metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Colombia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Colombia and selected international comparisons, based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The analytic figures (means, proficiency shares by levels, correlations, and variance explained) are produced using PISA’s complex sampling design and standard OECD/IEA estimation procedures for international comparisons. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name(s) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the specific weight fields cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Analysts using the underlying PISA microdata should apply the official PISA student sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the database when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals, and should follow the PISA Reader’s Guide for plausible-value and variance estimation conventions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided factsheet is a descriptive results summary and does not report an explicit plausible-values (PV) estimation procedure or any PV-specific analysis pipeline. It also does not document a missing-data handling strategy (e.g., listwise deletion, multiple imputation) for the reported estimates. This is therefore a reporting gap for methodological transparency in the excerpted text, even though PISA’s underlying technical documentation would normally specify these details.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Colombia sample as 7,804 students in 262 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 586,700 15-year-olds (an estimated 73% of the total 15-year-old population). The excerpt does not describe additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items, specific creative-thinking task completion thresholds), so the filtering criteria beyond the stated completion of the assessment are not specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-old students in Colombia and compares it with the OECD average and selected countries/economies. PISA 2022 creative thinking is assessed with 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Colombia’s mean creative thinking score is 26 out of 60, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet reports that 55% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency) and 12% are top performers at Levels 5–6. It also highlights within-country patterns: socio-economic status is a strong predictor (explaining 13% of variation), girls outperform boys by 1.6 points, and relative strengths appear in written and visual expression tasks. The excerpt does not provide the underlying PV/missing-data estimation details, so methodological caveats must be taken from the broader PISA technical documentation.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As such, there is no student-level machine learning model, no explicit PV-handling or missing-data procedure described in the excerpt, and no target-variable-specific predictive performance metrics to tabulate. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and uses the outcome summary to document the assessment design and reported benchmarks.
